The CLI incrementally scans standard Claude and Codex JSONL stores, ignores unknown record shapes, and discards any record over 1 MiB through its newline before continuing with later records.

Normal CLI startup is throttled before any telemetry request or source scan. An unknown or rotated token resolves once to the platform's stable account ID; later startups inside the account's throttle window do neither. Explicit usage sync and the Claude Stop/SessionEnd hook still perform the incremental scan. Edit-hook push commands skip telemetry work.
Uploads are monotonic and idempotent. Run detail is retained for 30 days, then rolled into monthly numeric aggregates.

Uploads send only the tail: runs that ended after the last fully-successful sync, plus a 48h overlap for clock skew and sessions still open at sync time. The high-water mark advances only when no app errored, so a failed upload stays in the next window. benmore usage sync always resends everything as the repair path.

A run is identified by (run key, provider, model) and the run key hashes the agent session only, so one session whose working directory crossed app markers is coalesced into a single run before upload: counters sum and attribution goes to the app holding the most tokens. Runs with all-zero counters are not uploaded.

An app the account no longer has - a deleted app, or a throwaway worktree app whose .benmore/app marker survived - is skipped with a named warning on stderr rather than failing the sync. Live apps in the same sync still upload.
